findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) can attach error data to the wrong ID
findings.body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node ID. It dedupes the input, and when some IDs are cached and others are not, it builds the result from a cache dict plus an uncached dict (src/sentry/nodestore/base.py:183-204). So the order of `.values()` is not guaranteed to match `error_ids`, and duplicate error IDs make the lengths differ. Zipping by position can then pair the wrong `id` with the wrong title, message and timestamp. Look each one up by key instead: `events.get(node_id)` for every `(event_id, node_id)` pair.

findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay event timestamps (milliseconds)
findings.body: An error's `timestamp` comes from nodestore event data, which stores epoch seconds as a float. Replay recording events (rrweb) carry epoch milliseconds in `timestamp`. A seconds value is always smaller than a milliseconds value, so the `while` loop emits every error before the first breadcrumb and the intended chronological interleaving never happens. The summary Seer receives is then silently out of order. Convert one side, e.g. compare `error['timestamp'] * 1000` with `event.get('timestamp', 0)`, and add a test that uses realistic units.

findings.title: get_environment_info runs one recommended-event lookup per issue
findings.body: Both the GitHub and GitLab merged-PR comment builders now call `get_environment_info` for every issue in the list. Each call runs `issue.get_recommended_event()`, which is an eventstore/Snuba query, and then `get_environment()`. That makes the comment task N+1 over the issue list. The list is small today, but batching the lookups or reading environment data from the issues query that already exists would avoid the extra round-trips.

findings.title: Analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check
findings.body: `preprod_artifact.api.assemble` is recorded before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` check. Requests that are then rejected with 404 still count as assemble calls, which inflates the metric. If the goal is to measure real usage, move the record call after the feature check, or add an attribute that marks rejected calls.

findings.title: With the feature flag on, table widgets always render empty
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` gets `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData`. `tableResults`, `loading` and the field renderers are all ignored. Any org with the flag sees every table widget empty, with no data and no loading state. If this is a placeholder, keep the flag off for every org until real data is passed through.

findings.title: Boolean(normalizedDateRange) is always true
findings.body: `normalizeDateTimeParams` returns an object, so `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is always `true` and does not gate the query. Either drop the condition or check the field the code actually depends on, e.g. that `start`/`end` or `statsPeriod` is present.

findings.title: Hidden attributes still show when the search box is empty
findings.body: The `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` check only runs inside the search filter (lines 65-69). When `searchQuery.trim()` is empty, the early return at lines 61-63 hands back `sorted` as is, so `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` still appear in the default view, which is the view most users see. They only disappear once the user types something. Apply the hidden filter to `sorted` before the early return, for example `const sorted = sortAttributes(attributes).filter(a => !HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(a.name));`.

findings.title: Attribute-keys query no longer sends the selected environments
findings.body: Before this change, `useTraceItemAttributeKeys` sent `environment: selection.environments` to `/trace-items/attributes/`. The shared `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` now leaves it out, with the comment "environment left out intentionally as it's not supported". As a result, the attribute suggestions in Explore and Logs no longer follow the environment page filter. Does the endpoint really ignore `environment`? If it doesn't, users with an environment selected will now get keys from every environment.

findings.title: Query options from the old `useApiQuery` were dropped
findings.body: The old query passed `staleTime: 0, refetchOnWindowFocus: false, retry: false`. The new `useQuery` call passes none of these, so the client defaults now apply: failures may be retried, and the query may refetch when the window regains focus. Because `isLoading` now maps to `isFetching` (line 61), every background refetch also flips the search bar's attributes into the loading state. If the old behaviour was wanted, add those options back.

findings.title: Typo and missing space in story text
findings.body: "Below is the the most basic example" repeats "the". There is also no space between "requires" and `tableData`, and the same happens at line 57 before `TabularData` and at line 110 before `renderTableBodyCell`. All of these render as run-together words.

findings.title: Renamed class says "Spans" but its fixtures are error and transaction events
findings.body: The class is now called `OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEventsSpans`, but its `setUp` stores error events (`message`/`fingerprint`) and a `load_data("transaction")` event through the discover path (lines 1260-1309). It does not set up span data. The new logs test's comment (line 3087, "implemented almost exactly the same as spans") repeats the same wrong framing. Consider a name like `OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEventsDiscover`, or drop the rename.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 4.** Part 1 has two likely defects, both in the new error context for replay breadcrumb summaries. Error data is matched to error IDs by position over the nodestore get_multi result, whose order is not guaranteed. Error timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay event timestamps (milliseconds), so every error is emitted before the first breadcrumb. Smaller points: the PR-comment environment lookup does one query per issue; the preprod analytics event is recorded before the feature check; the table-widget path behind the flag renders empty; and one hook has a condition that is always true. The remaining changes (migration no-ops pointing to 0921, which exists; task deadlines; Flex refactors; the browser-report serializer; detector owner handling) looked fine.

**Batch 2 of 4.** I reviewed all 32 files in part 2. One finding should be fixed in this PR. In the span attributes drawer, `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are only hidden while the user is searching: the empty-search early return skips the new filter, so they still show in the default view (`attributes.tsx:61`).

The remaining findings are things to consider:
- **Environment filter dropped:** the attribute-keys refactor no longer sends the selected environments, so suggestions may stop following the environment page filter. I've asked whether the endpoint really ignores that parameter.
- **Query options dropped:** `retry`, `staleTime` and `refetchOnWindowFocus` are no longer set, so retries and refetch-on-focus now follow the client defaults.
- **Story text:** a repeated "the" and a few missing spaces in `tableWidgetVisualization.stories.tsx`.

The other Explore changes replace a visualize's list of y-axes with a single y-axis, across the toolbar, charts, analytics, sort and dashboard export. They looked internally consistent and I found nothing to flag in them. The new table widget and the layout swaps (`Flex` replacing local styled divs) also had no issues. I couldn't settle the environment and retry questions because I didn't read the default query client settings or the backend endpoint, so that contract is left open.

**Batch 3 of 4.** I found no defects in part 3. The PR body describes a "Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System", but this part is mostly unrelated work:

- **Layout refactors:** several styled flex wrappers are replaced with the `Flex` and `Flex.Item` components, with the same CSS.
- **Explore specs:** updated to match `Visualize` now taking a single y-axis. I checked them against `visualizes.tsx`: `fromJSON` now returns an array, and the spec assertions match.
- **Hook spec:** `useGetTraceItemAttributeValues.spec` follows the hook's new signature without `attributeKey`.
- **Replay AI summary tab:** it now finds the project from `replayRecord.project_id` instead of the URL. When the project can't be found it shows an error, where before it spun forever.
- **Backend tests:** they follow the source changes in other parts: the autofix default is now `off`, the PR comment format changed, the browser-report validation is new, and `max_segment_id` can be `None`.

I didn't run any tests; this was a read-only review.

**Batch 4 of 4.** Part 4 is test files only. I checked each test against the code it exercises:
- Replay summarize tests: the expected ordering in `get_request_data` matches `gen_request_data`.
- Detector owner tests: they match the `ActorField` validation and how the base validator handles owner on create and update.
- Delayed workflow tests: they build `dcg_to_slow_conditions` the same way production does.
- Ourlogs top-N test: its expected counts are right (top 5 are 60/50/40/30/20, so Other is 10).

One finding, a "consider": the renamed `OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEventsSpans` class tests error and transaction events, not spans.
